chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nuḍr ibn Suwayd from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): By what is a man considered a Muslim, making his marriage and inheritance permissible, and by what is his blood protected? He said: His blood is protected by Islam when he manifests it, and his marriage and inheritance become permissible. He is not contradictory to what we have mentioned, because whoever manifests enmity and elevation (al-Naṣb) towards the Family of the Messenger (peace be upon him) has not truly manifested Islam, but is at the peak of manifesting disbelief. And the report only included those who manifested Islam, and these (the Naṣāʾib) are excluded from it.

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِ الرَّسُولِ ص: the Family of the Messenger (peace be upon him)
key_terms.النَّصْبَ: al-Naṣb (elevation of the Umayyad caliphs and enmity towards Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.يَحْرُمُ دَمُهُ: his blood is protected (from being killed)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a Muslim's marriage and inheritance to be permissible according to the manifestation of faith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isṭibṣār clarifies the Shia doctrine of 'manifestation' (ẓuhūr) in determining religious status, distinguishing between nominal Islam and the substantive reality required for marriage and inheritance. It establishes that persistent enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt (al-Naṣb) invalidates the outward profession of faith, rendering such individuals effectively outside the fold of true Islam despite their public declaration.
